title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Dispatch Standing and the Classification of a Call
content:
## Standing to dispatch

A demand call is dispatched under the program only while the program stands active or pending renewal; a
suspended or expired program is served at the published walk-up rates with payment taken before the
technician is released. A call at an account over the tier's credit limit is held until the office
releases it, and a call outside regular hours is accepted only where the tier accepts after-hours
dispatch.

## Classification at intake

Every accepted call is classified at intake as routine, priority, emergency or critical, and the
classification fixes the response guarantee: the tier's routine, priority, emergency and critical
response hours respectively, counted in elapsed hours from the moment the call was accepted, without
regard to office hours.

A call is classified as emergency only where the fault leaves the building without heating or cooling,
floods, or threatens equipment damage; comfort complaints and requests to advance a scheduled visit are
routine however urgently they are stated, and the desk never reclassifies a call on the caller's
insistence alone. A critical classification is available only at the two highest tiers and only at a
building whose use class is a data centre or a medical office.

## The same rules, condition by condition

| What the record shows | The call under the Demand Service Rate Programs |
|---|---|
| the program stands active or pending renewal | is dispatched under the program |
| the program stands suspended or expired | is served at the published walk-up rates, payment taken before the technician is released |
| the open balance stands over the tier's credit limit | is held until the office releases it |
| the hours fall outside regular hours and the tier accepts after-hours dispatch | is accepted |
| the hours fall outside regular hours and the tier does not accept after-hours dispatch | is not accepted |

The queue position each program carries, and the response hours each classification carries, are those
published for that program.

### Points of judgement

- A tenant complaint of discomfort is routine, however it is put, unless the fault leaves the building
  without heating or cooling, floods, or threatens equipment damage.
- A critical classification at a building that is neither a data centre nor a medical office is not
  available, whatever the program.
- The after-hours column governs acceptance alone; where the tier accepts after-hours dispatch the
  classification is still made on the fault.
